items.q: Excess fertiliser runoff into a lake causes:
items.explain: Nutrients drive algal blooms, and their decay depletes oxygen.
items.explainAf: Voedingstowwe veroorsaak alge-uitbrake, en die ontbinding daarvan put suurstof uit.

items.q: CFCs damage the ozone layer by:
items.explain: Chlorine from CFCs catalytically breaks down ozone.
items.explainAf: Chloor uit CFK's breek osoon katalities af.

items.explain: Sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides form acids in the atmosphere.
items.explainAf: Swaveldioksied en stikstofoksiede vorm sure in die atmosfeer.

items.q: A keystone species is one that:
options: Has a large effect on its ecosystem relative to its abundance
optionsAf: ’n Groot effek op sy ekosisteem het relatief tot sy talrykheid
items.explain: Keystone species, such as some predators, shape the community out of proportion to their numbers.
items.explainAf: Sleutelspesies, soos sommige roofdiere, vorm die gemeenskap buite verhouding tot hul getalle.

items.q: Which is an in situ conservation method?
items.explain: In situ conservation protects species in their natural habitat.
items.explainAf: In situ-bewaring beskerm spesies in hul natuurlike habitat.

items.q: Which is an ex situ conservation method?
items.explain: Ex situ conservation stores species outside their natural habitat.
items.explainAf: Ex situ-bewaring stoor spesies buite hul natuurlike habitat.

items.q: The rapid growth of algae in water caused by too many nutrients such as fertilisers.
items.qAf: Die vinnige groei van alge in water wat deur te veel voedingstowwe soos kunsmis veroorsaak word.

items.q: The process by which fertile land becomes desert.
items.qAf: Die proses waardeur vrugbare grond woestyn word.

items.q: A plant or animal brought into an area where it does not naturally occur, which spreads and harms local species.
items.qAf: ’n Plant of dier wat in ’n gebied ingebring word waar dit nie natuurlik voorkom nie, wat versprei en plaaslike spesies benadeel.

items.q: Hunting animals illegally, for example rhinos for their horns.
items.qAf: Om diere onwettig te jag, byvoorbeeld renosters vir hul horings.

items.text: Burning fossil fuels releases sulfur dioxide, which forms [[]] rain. Plastic waste that breaks into tiny pieces is called [[]].
items.textAf: Om fossielbrandstowwe te verbrand, stel swaeldioksied vry, wat [[]]reën vorm. Plastiekafval wat in klein stukkies breek, word [[]] genoem.

items.q: Alien plants such as wattle use more water than many indigenous plants.
items.qAf: Uitheemse plante soos wattel gebruik meer water as baie inheemse plante.
items.explain: True. That is why the Working for Water programme removes them from catchment areas.
items.explainAf: Waar. Dit is waarom die Werk vir Water-program hulle uit opvanggebiede verwyder.

items.q: Food security means that a country produces more food than it can eat.
items.qAf: Voedselsekerheid beteken dat ’n land meer kos produseer as wat dit kan eet.
items.explain: False. Food security means all people always have access to enough safe, nutritious food.
items.explainAf: Onwaar. Voedselsekerheid beteken dat alle mense altyd toegang het tot genoeg veilige, voedsame kos.

items.q: Explain how fertiliser running off farmland into a dam can cause fish to die.
items.qAf: Verduidelik hoe kunsmis wat van landbougrond in ’n dam afloop, kan veroorsaak dat visse doodgaan.
points: Nutrients cause algae to grow rapidly (eutrophication).
When the algae die, decomposers break them down and use up the oxygen in the water.
The fish die from lack of oxygen.
pointsAf: Wanneer die alge doodgaan, breek ontbinders hulle af en gebruik die suurstof in die water op.
Die visse gaan dood weens ’n gebrek aan suurstof.
